news.title: Morocco U15 to World Cup Second Round After Five Straight Wins
news.lede: Rabat – Morocco’s under-15 national football team has qualified for the second round of the World Cup finals after winning all five of its opening-round matches. The young Atlas Lions secured qualification with a convincing 5-1 victory over Liberia on Monday, extending a winning run that began with victories over the Philippines, Costa Rica, and Belize before further success against Curaçao. Morocco settled the match early, with Saïd Noufii scoring a hat-trick in the opening 10 minutes. He found the net in the fourth, sixth, and 10th minutes, putting Liberia under immediate pressure.

news.title: Who is Luis de la Fuente? Spain's FIFA World Cup-winning manager wins Men's Coach of the Year award at Ballon d'Or event
news.lede: Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente was named Men's Coach of the Year at the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony in London on Monday, after guiding the national team to the FIFA World Cup title earlier this year. The 65-year-old became the third recipient of the award, succeeding Paris Saint-Germain manager Luis Enrique, who won it in 2025. De la Fuente received the recognition following Spain's 1-0 victory over Argentina in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final in New Jersey on July 19. Ferran Torres scored the decisive goal in the 106th minute as Spain secured their second World Cup title, 16 years after their maiden triumph in 2010.

news.title: Players Who Defined an Entire World Cup
news.lede: The World Cup has never felt like just another football competition. Every four years, it seems to produce players who step out of the ordinary and leave something lasting behind. It is not always the top scorer or even the captain of the winning side who stands out, but often the one who carries their team through the pressure and expectation.
